title: 6 Habits That Slowly Separate You From God
paragraphs: 6 Habits That Slowly Separate You From God
It rarely starts with rebellion.
It starts with drift.
Not a loud denial. Not a public scandal. Just a few quiet habits that make your heart colder while your life still looks “fine.”
And that’s the danger.
Here are 6 habits that slowly separate you from God:

1. Praying only when you’re in trouble
Some people don’t want God. They just want relief.
So they run to Him in pain, then forget Him in peace.
But prayer was never meant to be your panic button. It is your lifeline.
“Pray without ceasing.” (1 Thessalonians 5:17)

2. Feeding on everything except Scripture
You can scroll for hours, binge voices all day, absorb the world nonstop—
then wonder why your soul feels weak.
A starving spirit cannot stand in a tempting world.
“Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.” (Matthew 4:4)

3. Making peace with “small” sin
A little lust. A little dishonesty. A little bitterness. A little compromise.
We rename it so we don’t have to repent of it.
But tolerated sin never stays small. It grows roots.
“Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vineyards.” (Song of Solomon 2:15)

4. Living too busy to worship
When everything is urgent, God becomes optional.
Work. Money. Deadlines. Notifications.
Your schedule starts preaching a sermon your mouth would never say:
“I have time for everything except the One who gave me life.”
“Seek first the kingdom of God…” (Matthew 6:33)

5. Staying around voices that normalize compromise
Who shapes your appetite?
Some friendships don’t pull you toward Christ—they slowly numb your conviction.
Not every voice in your life deserves a seat at your table.
“Bad company ruins good morals.” (1 Corinthians 15:33)

6. Delaying obedience
You know what God said.
Forgive. Let it go. Cut it off. Return. Confess. Surrender.
But delayed obedience is still disobedience.
And every delay hardens the heart a little more.
“Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.” (Hebrews 3:15)
But here’s what we miss:
The greatest tragedy is not that these habits exist.
It’s that we keep them longer than we keep running back to Jesus.
Listen to me carefully—drift is real, but so is grace.
You may feel far from God right now. Numb. Dry. Convicted. Ashamed.
Come back anyway.

Jesus is not waiting to crush the repentant. He is ready to receive them.
The cross is proof that God does not save perfect people. He saves returning people.
He saves sinners who stop hiding and start surrendering.
So repent.

Not tomorrow.
Now.

Open your Bible again.
Pray again.
Worship again.
Obey again.
And let Christ pull you close where your soul belongs.
“Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you.” (James 4:8)
